Look up, Wanderer. Beyond this moon, the lights over Janira Prime are not stars. They are the engines of an army that believes surrounding a world is the same as possessing it. Tonight, we will teach them the difference.

I know what those ships awaken in you. You have seen their colours above Earth. You have heard Hawthorne announce victories as though every life beneath him were a number on a chart. You have already lost a home to that voice. I will not ask you to pretend that it does not hurt.

The people sheltering behind us have carried children through burning ports, crossed systems in damaged freighters, and left names unanswered on silent channels. They did not come here because they were weak. They came because they refused to surrender the people beside them.

And now Terra Imperia has followed them. Hawthorne would have us believe there is nowhere left to stand. He would turn every sanctuary into another border, every neighbour into an enemy, and every frightened survivor into an obedient subject.

But Janira Prime is not his reward for taking Sol. Its violet fields were growing before he raised his first banner. Its cities belong to the hands that built them. Its future belongs to those who will live there, not to a man who has never walked its streets.

I am Hak Chompjak, and I will defend my people. Yet hear me clearly: this is greater than my throne. If the crown must fall so that a family in Karribassa may see another dawn, then let the crown fall. A ruler is replaceable. A people is not.

To the Federation crews here on Janira I: you have not ceased to be a nation because your capital changed. Your courage did not remain on Earth. It came with you, aboard every vessel that chose rescue over retreat.

To Vishara and the Erisian Resistance: the empire that was stolen from you does not define what you can become. Today you fly beside those who were once strangers. Let that choice, freely made, speak louder than any puppet's decree.

And to you, Wanderer: you began this journey alone in the snow. Look at the company you have gathered. Worlds now answer a banner you chose, and people follow you because you gave them a reason to believe that tomorrow could be different.

We do not have to break their entire fleet in one glorious charge. We must keep our formation, protect the ships that cannot protect themselves, and find a path through that blockade. Courage is not throwing lives away. Courage is bringing them home.

Their captains will see different hulls, different languages, different histories. Let them. When they fire upon one of us, they will discover that they have challenged all of us. Today our differences are not cracks in a wall. They are the foundations of an alliance.

If fear finds you in your cockpit, let it sit beside you. Check your instruments. Listen for your wingmates. Take the next breath and make the next good decision. No one here needs you to be fearless. We need you to stay with us.

In a moment, I will send a light above this refuge. Every ship still waiting in the dark will see it. Not a weapon aimed at our own sky, but a promise: Janira has not fallen silent, and no one defending it will fight alone.

Ready your ships. Call your crews. Carry the names of those you have lost, and leave room among them for the living you intend to save. When we lift from this moon, we fly for every world that has been told resistance is impossible.

There is Janira Prime. There are our people. Between us stands Terra Imperia, and beyond it waits a dawn they have no right to steal. With me, Wanderer. Let the sky remember that we came for one another.
